lead: An app shares data by sending a content:// URI in an intent with a temporary read grant. It does not copy files into a public folder or reveal a private path. The receiver asks Android for bytes through ContentResolver. This is how a report app sends a PDF to a viewer, a photo app sends an image to chat, and a receipt is attached to email. The grant is narrow: one URI, read only, for one activity. Only a few universities teach this advanced topic.
prereq: You need Chapter 4.4 for content URIs and resolvers, and Unit 2 for implicit intents.

sections.h3: Share with an intent, not a folder

blocks.text: An implicit intent names an action, not a target class. ACTION_SEND shares one item; ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE shares many. Call setType("application/pdf") so Android lists apps that accept that MIME type. Text goes in Intent.EXTRA_TEXT. A file goes in Intent.EXTRA_STREAM as a content:// URI, never as a File. For many files, put an ArrayList<Uri> in the same extra. A wrong MIME type can hide the right receiver. Set the MIME type with setType() so Android can match receivers; putExtra() later does not change it. Do not call setData() after setType(), because setData() clears the type (and setType() clears the data).

Intent.createChooser(send, "Share report") opens the system share sheet; the string is its heading. The chooser does not copy the file. The selected app receives the same extras and URI. The receiver calls getContentResolver().openInputStream(uri). This design exists because each app has a private data folder; guessing another app's path is unsafe and often impossible. It also lets Android apply a temporary grant instead of a broad folder permission. The URI points to the provider, not to a raw directory.

Your app must turn a private File into a shareable URI. Use FileProvider, an AndroidX subclass of ContentProvider. Add a <provider> tag. Set android:name="androidx.core.content.FileProvider", android:authorities="com.example.reportapp.fileprovider", android:exported="false", and android:grantUriPermissions="true". Inside the <provider> tag add <meta-data android:name="android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS" android:resource="@xml/file_paths" />. This line connects the provider to file_paths.xml; without it getUriForFile throws IllegalArgumentException ("Failed to find configured root that contains ..."). The authority is a name you invent; it must match the string in code. exported="false" stops other apps from browsing the provider. grantUriPermissions="true" lets an intent give a temporary pass to one URI.

Add res/xml/file_paths.xml. It maps a public name to a private folder: <paths><files-path name="reports" path="reports/" /></paths>. Here reports/ is inside getFilesDir(). Then call Uri uri = FileProvider.getUriForFile(this, "com.example.reportapp.fileprovider", file);. If file is .../files/reports/report.pdf, the URI is content://com.example.reportapp.fileprovider/reports/report.pdf. The real path stays hidden. A file:// URI is refused from Android 7 (API 24): sharing it throws FileUriExposedException.

A content URI alone is not access. Add send.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION). This flag travels with the intent and lets the chosen receiver read that URI. Without it, the receiver's openInputStream call fails with SecurityException.

The grant lasts while the receiving activity is alive. It covers only the URI in the intent. It does not let the receiver list the reports folder, read other files, or write. If you share many files, add the flag once to the ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE intent; each URI in EXTRA_STREAM gets the grant. The receiver opens the stream, copies or displays it, and closes it. The sender keeps ownership of the file. A mail app may attach a copy; a viewer may only display it. Do not promise permanent access in an answer. A grant is not a password and not a file permission on disk.

spec.title: Sharing a file safely
spec.aria: A report.pdf of 1.5 MB (1572864 bytes) goes through FileProvider to a content URI, then into an ACTION_SEND intent with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION, and the PDF viewer calls openInputStream to read exactly 1572864 bytes.

examples.question: A report app has report.pdf of 1.5 MB in .../files/reports/. Its authority is com.example.reportapp.fileprovider. Write the sharing code for any PDF viewer. State what the viewer may do.
steps: Confirm the <provider> tag contains <meta-data android:name="android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS" android:resource="@xml/file_paths" />, which connects the provider to file_paths.xml. Then confirm the folder is declared there: <files-path name="reports" path="reports/" />.
Build the File object for report.pdf. Its size is 1.5 MB = 1572864 bytes.
Call Uri uri = FileProvider.getUriForFile(this, "com.example.reportapp.fileprovider", file);. The result is content://com.example.reportapp.fileprovider/reports/report.pdf.
Build the intent: Intent send = new Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND); send.setType("application/pdf"); send.putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_STREAM, uri); send.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION);.
The viewer may call openInputStream(uri) and read exactly 1572864 bytes of that one file. It cannot list the reports folder or write. The grant ends with the receiving activity.
examples.answer: The viewer gets a temporary read grant to one content URI for report.pdf of 1.5 MB (1572864 bytes); it cannot browse the folder or write.

traps: Passing a file:// URI (for example Uri.fromFile(file)) in EXTRA_STREAM, or as the intent data, throws FileUriExposedException on Android 7 (API 24) and later. Always pass the content:// URI from FileProvider instead.
Leaving out FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION gives the receiver SecurityException.
A grant is temporary and per URI; it is not permanent folder access.
The manifest authority and the getUriForFile authority must match exactly.
Forgetting setType, or using the wrong MIME type, can leave the chooser empty.

quiz.q: Which extra carries a file URI?
Why use a content:// URI instead of a file path?
quiz.a: It hides the private path and allows a temporary read grant.

quiz.q: Authority is com.example.reportapp.fileprovider and the file is .../files/reports/report.pdf. What URI is returned?
A receiver gets SecurityException when opening a shared PDF. What is the likely missing flag?
Why can the receiver read report.pdf but not list the reports folder?
quiz.a: The grant is for one URI only, not for the whole provider.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern Android adds scoped storage and the Storage Access Framework, where the user picks a document and the app receives a persistable URI permission. Photo Picker reduces broad gallery access. Industry share sheets use these same intents and grants. Search for FileProvider, scoped storage, and ACTION_SEND.
